decision: Qualified source-level PASS on statutory mismatch; parent owns publication decision
scope: Initial document validity for an EFP containing only the specified single-shot smooth-bore long guns for hunters/sports shooters. Not weapons-possession authorisation, not an identified invalid trip or issued pass.

history.assessment: Original five-year rule expressly allowed ten years for category D. This historic exception is context, not current EU permission.

history.provision: Article 1(1)(e), replacing the entire Article 1(4); Article 2(1)
history.assessment: Personally read entire authentic replacement and deadline: maximum five years, extendable; no former ten-year category-D exception; due 28 July 2010. The official Cellar manifestation returned HTML/XML, which was read as text.
Later replacement/codification retains the five-year maximum; 2017 is not the earliest origin of this missed update.

national.provision: Section 33(1), whole current provision personally read
national.assessment: Express initial ten-year duration in the specified cohort, followed separately by two possible five-year extensions. Merely allowing extension under EU law does not textually establish that an initial ten-year document is itself a five-year issue plus a separately assessed extension.

adverse: Current individual limitations, periodic weapons-authorisation review, withdrawal and EU-consistent interpretation remain material. A document-duration discrepancy does not establish unlawful weapons possession.
Parent independently read BVA/general five-year guidance; other current official guidance describes the ten-year exception. Mixed guidance prevents claiming universal national practice.
No individual pass, administrative decision, failed travel or actual reliance was identified.

officialPracticeCorroboration.assessment: Actual official indexed full service text, crawled two days before snapshot, describes five years and the ten-year single-loader exception. Its English translation is broader/imprecise compared with the statutory smooth-bore cohort, so the statute controls scope.

Official district service text expressly describes ten years for hunters/sports shooters with only single-shot smooth-bore long guns; displayed source date 24 October 2025. Not evidence of an issued pass.

recognitionSearch.result: No precise prior published criticism of this EU-versus-German validity mismatch located in bounded searches. Statute reproductions, ordinary ten-year guidance, and unrelated cases are not exact recognition. No first-discovery claim.
